key_insight: AI-assisted simulations reveal how SrTiO₃ grain-boundary composition and atomic structure control electronic states, electric fields, and local polarization.
engineering_relevance: The findings offer a route toward engineering oxide-perovskite interfaces, but do not directly demonstrate improved solar-cell performance.
method: Combine Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential.
Map stable grain-boundary structures across chemical potentials and boundary geometries.
Use density functional theory and electrostatic analysis to characterize electronic and polar behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ten stable Σ5(310)[001] structures in four motif families and four electronic regimes, with structural exploration extended to two other grain boundaries.
watch_item: Experimental validation and transferability to photovoltaic perovskites are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
